clue.text: Hard to have pained expression, as Eliza might have been heard to say to 23?

definitions.text: as Eliza might have been heard to say to 23?
definitions.note: an elocution phrase said to a cow, and 23 is ALDERNEY, a breed of dairy cow

blocks.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
to have something is to own it
ow is what you say when hurt

explanation.surface: Someone finds it hard to wear a pained look, in the voice of Eliza Doolittle.
explanation.walkthrough: In Pygmalion and My Fair Lady, Eliza Doolittle practises the vowel drill 'How now, brown cow'; an Alderney is a cow, so this is what she would say to one.
explanation.definitionFit: The elocution drill addresses a brown cow, and an Alderney is a breed of cow, so the greeting suits it.

clue.text: See 25 across
Golfer, awfully kind, used to be on circuit

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of kind are mangled
going on a circuit means going round, so the past-tense word goes round the rest

blocks.note: used to be is the past tense was
the letters of kind, taken as written, are the ones mangled

explanation.surface: A golfer who was once nice used to play on the tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circuit' suggests the professional tour; here it means going around the other letters. Lanny Wadkins is an American major winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanny Wadkins won the 1977 US PGA Championship and played many Ryder Cups for the United States.

clue.text: Centre of 26: editor's given 12 26 at that T

blocks.note: 26-across is MONTHS, and its centre is everything but the first and last letters
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor
twelve months make a year, written as the article a with Y, the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: An editor fills a page with numbered cross-references to say when something happened.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers are not entries to look up together: '12 26' is twelve months, a year, giving A and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: On the day means at the very time in question, so it stands for at that time.

clue.text: Women being pulled in outskirts of Turin (Urbs gemina)

indicators.note: the women and the towing are placed inside the frame the city name provides
the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the first and last letters are used

blocks.note: the Italian city's name supplies just its edge letters
W is the standard abbreviation for women
something being pulled is in tow

explanation.surface: Women are dragged into the edges of an Italian city, with a Latin tag that sounds like a guidebook caption.
explanation.walkthrough: Urbs gemina is Latin for 'twin city'; in the UK a twin town is one formally paired with a foreign town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase translates literally as a paired or twinned city, which is what a twin town is.

clue.text: Capital Burns hero I Glasgow kiss: we'll hang about — hang about for a T

definitions.note: a request to wait, phrased in terms of a short time

indicators.note: the pronoun hangs around the other pieces, enclosing them

blocks.note: the pronoun we, with will meaning it is the subject that acts
capital means excellent, A1, written AI
Tam o' Shanter is the hero of a Robert Burns poem
taken as written
a Glasgow kiss is a headbutt, so to nut

explanation.surface: A Scottish scene of a hero and a headbutt, followed by an impatient request to wait.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-class, so 'capital' gives AI. A Glasgow kiss is a headbutt, a nut in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking someone to hang on is to ask them to pause, and the minute is the short time asked for.

clue.text: Brown's up on half of Teutonic language, he may remind you

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the brown word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: dun is a dull greyish brown
the Teutonic language is German, and its first half is three letters

explanation.surface: Somebody named Brown upset over a Germanic language reminds you of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname; it is the colour dun.
explanation.definitionFit: One who nudges gives a gentle prompt, so is a person who jogs your memory.

clue.text: Not a short T, in-house

blocks.note: reads as any long stretch of time, but points to the saying that a week is a long time in politics
reads as internal to a company, but means in the House of Commons, the world of politics

explanation.surface: A period that is not short, within an organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Wilson, the British Prime Minister, said 'A week is a long time in politics'; the House is the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilson's famous remark says that a single week counts as a long period for those in Parliament.

clue.text: Sing "Fa": the resort for notes after closing T

definitions.note: a bank's deposit box for banknotes once the branch has shut

indicators.note: to re-sort letters is to sort them afresh into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, part of the letters to re-sort
the sol-fa note, taken as written
taken as written, the last of the letters to re-sort

explanation.surface: Singing a musical note becomes the last resort for notes after closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday place and 'notes' like music; resort is re-sort, and the notes are banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: A night safe is a slot in a bank wall where customers deposit cash when the bank is closed.

clue.text: Current intelligence not in bed with T

blocks.note: someone who is not in bed is up
throughout this puzzle T stands for time, and a date is a point in time

explanation.surface: A report on someone's alertness and bed habits, with a cryptic letter thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle's theme letter T always stands for TIME or a kind of time; here a date.
explanation.definitionFit: An update is the latest news, so current intelligence in the sense of fresh information.

clue.text: What's laid on large scale road south, say, as a core

indicators.note: the other pieces form the core of the word for large, sitting in its middle

blocks.note: something on a large scale is big
RD is the standard abbreviation for road
S is the compass abbreviation
say introduces an example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: Something being laid on a big scale, like a road surface with a southern core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid' suggests tarmac or paving on the road; it is what a hen lays.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds lay eggs, so a bird's egg is literally something laid.

clue.text: T with a long T wasting nothing in 12's T: the key to running a busy life

definitions.text: the key to running a busy life

indicators.note: wasting something loses it, so the zero letter is dropped
the long stretch of time goes into the remains of the other word

blocks.note: throughout this puzzle T stands for time, here taken as the word itself
12-down is AT THE MOMENT, so its kind of time is a moment
nothing is zero, the letter O
a long time is an age, kept with its article as an age

explanation.surface: A tangle of times and moments presented as advice on handling a hectic schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The article belongs to the piece: 'a long T' gives AN AGE, which sits inside MOMENT once its O has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Organising one's hours efficiently is the skill that keeps a hectic schedule under control.

clue.text: Those people sign in attorney T now

indicators.note: the people and the sign go inside the abbreviation for attorney

blocks.note: Att. is an abbreviation for attorney
those people are them
an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: Some people sign a document in front of a lawyer right now.
explanation.definitionFit: At the moment means at present, at this time, the same as now.

clue.text: T going west in form of lottery

blocks.note: throughout this puzzle T stands for a time, here an instant
W is the compass abbreviation for west
taken as written

explanation.surface: Time heading west inside some kind of lottery game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going west' looks like a phrase for dying or a reversal, but 'west' just gives its letter and 'going' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant win is a scratchcard-style game where the prize is revealed at once, a common kind of lottery.

clue.text: From Tallahassee to Atlanta, say, take off unwillingly?

definitions.note: take off is slang for dying, and doing so without a will

indicators.note: say signals that the travel word only sounds like the answer, with the R dropped in British speech

blocks.note: going from Florida's capital to Georgia's is going between states

explanation.surface: A trip from Florida to Georgia, perhaps a reluctant flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests a plane leaving; it is slang for dying. Without a will is 'unwillingly', a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dies intestate dies without having made a will.

clue.text: What's on hand for ladies, or a king's admitted

indicators.note: the king is let in between the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A question about what a lady has on her hand, perhaps a ring, or a king being let in.
explanation.walkthrough: The vegetable is also called ladies' fingers, and fingers are on the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is known as ladies' fingers, and fingers are what one has on a hand.

clue.text: Hot stuff: a writer in dilapidated car, parking yards away

indicators.note: the article and the writing tool sit inside the remains of the old car
away means the parking and yards letters are taken out

blocks.note: a jalopy is a battered old car
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
Y is an abbreviation for yards
taken as written
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Something hot, perhaps an author, sits in a wrecked car with the parking moved away.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalapeño is a Mexican chilli pepper, so hot stuff in the spicy sense.

clue.text: T's partner at the Guardian put right back

indicators.note: back tells you to read the word for correcting copy from the end

blocks.note: at a newspaper such as the Guardian, putting copy right is editing it

explanation.surface: Someone's partner at the newspaper is set straight again.
explanation.walkthrough: T is time in this puzzle, and the proverb pairs it: time and tide wait for no man.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'time and tide wait for no man' makes tide the traditional companion of time.

clue.text: Opener spotted hexahedron, going for it!

blocks.note: a door is what you open to get in
a die is a six-faced cube marked with spots

explanation.surface: Someone opening a spotted cube cheers as they take a risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' suggests a cricket batsman or a can opener; it is simply a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A do-or-die attempt is an all-out effort with everything at stake, like going for it.

clue.text: In T make uniform (back of arm) and get up

indicators.note: back here asks for the gun's name to be written from its end to its start

blocks.note: an arm is a weapon, and the Luger is a German pistol
to get up out of bed or a chair is to arise

explanation.surface: A drill instructor orders recruits to march in step, smarten their uniforms, mind their arms and stand up.
explanation.walkthrough: T stands for TIME throughout this puzzle, so the definition reads 'in time make uniform'. 'Arm' looks like the limb, which the brackets play up; it is a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: To regularise is to make something regular, even and steady, as a beat kept in time is.

clue.text: One groove in which to get on over press

indicators.note: the on and the over go into the one-plus-groove frame

blocks.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a rut is a groove worn into a surface
taken as written
O is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A single groove in which a record is pressed and played.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron out creases is to press clothes flat with an iron.

clue.text: Deprive of top day of victory

blocks.note: a star is someone at the top
VE Day is Victory in Europe day, 8 May 1945

explanation.surface: Taking away the best part of a victory celebration day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deprive of top' reads like removing a first letter, but 'top' is the star.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve someone of something is to keep it from them, withholding what they need.

clue.text: He's suave (Sade?), open to debate in store and an extended T on hill

blocks.note: a store is a shop
a moot point is one open to debate
an extended time is an era
a tor is a rocky hill, common in Dartmoor place names

explanation.surface: A smooth charmer, perhaps of de Sade's sort, is a matter for argument in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Sade is the singer whose 1984 hit was 'Smooth Operator'; the Marquis de Sade is the false scent. The debating word sits after the S of the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth operator is a charming, suave man, and the phrase is the title of Sade's best-known song.

clue.text: T passes away with top swap

indicators.note: the two top letters change places, the first and second swapped

blocks.note: to pass away is to die, so dies

explanation.surface: Time runs out after the leader is swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: In this puzzle T means time; the Ides were dates in the Roman calendar, as in the Ides of March.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides were fixed days in each Roman month, a calendar term for a specific date.

clue.text: Feature of Channel 5 withdrawn from every land broadcast

indicators.note: the Roman five is taken out of the phrase that follows
seed broadcast is scattered widely, so the remaining letters are scattered and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the phrase the numeral is removed from
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Something on the TV station Channel 5 is pulled from broadcast everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel 5' reads as the British TV channel; the Channel is the English Channel and the 5 is V.
explanation.definitionFit: Alderney is one of the Channel Islands, a geographical feature of the English Channel.

clue.text: Silverback T

blocks.note: first meaning: silver is the medal for the runner-up
... meaning: to back a proposal is to ... it
third meaning: in this puzzle T is time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Silverback' reads as the gorilla; split it into silver and back and each, like T, is a separate meaning of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Second is a runner-up's place, a verb meaning to support a motion, and a sixtieth of a minute.

clue.text: Love the Ben Hur novel: book out at last T in 5

definitions.note: 5-down is WAIT A MINUTE, so the last time in its terms is the last minute

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement
the book abbreviation is put out of the fodder

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter of these words is used
B is a standard abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A romance reading of the Ben-Hur novel, with the book finally out.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 1-down, giving ELEVENTH HOUR. 'Novel' looks like Lew Wallace's book; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh hour is the latest possible moment, the same idea as the last minute.

clue.text: Ts having T? This I abandoned

definitions.note: plural: periods of time, here calendar divisions of the year

indicators.note: the I is abandoned, left out of the word before it

blocks.note: throughout this puzzle T stands for a time, here Mon., the short form of Monday
taken as written, the word that loses its letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about times having a time, then someone gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme letter T stands for time throughout; Mon. is the calendar short form of Monday, a day being a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Months are units of time on the calendar, so they are times in the puzzle's shorthand.
